title: A Phone Call Home About the New Apartment
script: Dara: [cheerful] Hi Mom, I finally have a free evening, so I thought I'd call and tell you about the apartment.
Mother: [warmly] I was hoping you'd call. How is everything going with the move?
Dara: [tired but happy] Mostly good. Boxes are still everywhere, but I found my favorite pan yesterday, so that felt like a small victory.
Mother: That's how it always is. You unpack the kitchen last but need it first.
Dara: Exactly. I've been eating a lot of simple meals, rice and eggs mostly, until things settle down.
Mother: Have you set up a routine yet, or is it still chaos every day?
Dara: Getting there. I wake up earlier now because the commute is longer than my old place.
Mother: [concerned] How much longer exactly? I don't want you exhausted every single day.
Dara: About twenty minutes more, so it's manageable. I actually use the extra time to plan my day.
Mother: What about the neighborhood? Do you like it so far?
Dara: [warmly] I really do. There's a small market nearby, and I've already started buying vegetables there instead of the big store.
Mother: That sounds lovely. Fresh food always makes a place feel more like home.
Dara: It does. I also met one neighbor, an older woman who waters plants in the hallway every morning.
Mother: Did you talk to her much?
Dara: A little. She told me where the good bakery is, and I already went there twice this week.
Mother: [teasing] Twice in one week? Some things about you never change.
Dara: Guilty. Anyway, I'm slowly making it feel like my own space, one box at a time.
Mother: That takes time, sweetheart. Don't rush it. A home is built slowly, not all at once.
Dara: [gently] That's a nice way to think about it. I'll call again once the living room is finally organized.
Mother: I'll hold you to that. I love you, and I'm proud of you for handling this on your own.
Dara: [warmly] Love you too, Mom. Talk soon.
